definitions.explanation: The preserved remains or traces of ancient organisms found in rock. Also used figuratively to describe something outdated or behind the times.

examples.japanese: {恐竜|きょうりゅう}の{化石|かせき}が{見|み}つかった。
この{地層|ちそう}からは{貝|かい}の{化石|かせき}が{多|おお}く{出|で}る。
examples.english: Many shell fossils come out of this geological layer.

examples.japanese: {博物館|はくぶつかん}には{数百万年前|すうひゃくまんねんまえ}の{化石|かせき}が{展示|てんじ}されており、{子|こ}どもたちに{大人気|だいにんき}だ。
examples.english: The museum displays fossils from millions of years ago, and they are very popular with children.

notes:
Also used figuratively to describe something hopelessly outdated, as in {化石|かせき}みたいな{考|かんが}え{方|かた} (fossil-like way of thinking). The compound {化石|かせき}{燃料|ねんりょう} (fossil fuel) is frequently encountered in news about energy and the environment.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{化石|かせき}を{発掘|はっくつ}する: to excavate a fossil
・{化石|かせき}{燃料|ねんりょう}: fossil fuel
・{恐竜|きょうりゅう}の{化石|かせき}: dinosaur fossil
